ai.title: SDK filesystem interface migrates to async promises
ai.summary: CodebuffFileSystem type in common/src/types/filesystem.ts now exclusively accepts fs.promises methods (exists, mkdir, readdir, readFile, stat, writeFile), removing all synchronous fs.*Sync counterparts. Core utilities like getProjectFileTree, parseGitignore, and ensureDirectoryExists in common/src/util/file.ts and common/src/project-file-tree.ts were converted to async functions returning Promises to match the new interface. This change impacts the SDK core, CLI (npm-app/src/cli.ts), and Evals (evals/scaffolding.ts), requiring callers to await filesystem operations. Synchronous helpers like getCurrentChatDirSync were retained or introduced in npm-app/src/chat-storage.ts to preserve non-blocking UI threads where async propagation is impractical.

eli5.text: The assistant's file-reading helper (the part that explores your project folder and lists your files) now does its work in the background instead of pausing everything while it looks. This applies to the core engine, the command-line tool, and the evaluation test system, so operations like scanning directories, checking file stats, and reading gitignore rules no longer freeze the interface when they touch a slow disk or network drive. You would notice the experience stays responsive during project indexing, but only on versions dated November 4, 2025 or later; older builds still run those same file operations the old synchronous way.

ai.summary: Version 0.6.0 of @codebuff/sdk ships as a cumulative release bundling CLI enhancements, agent-runtime refactorings, and web routing changes since 0.5.12. Notable additions include the PLAN agent mode with Build Fast/Max buttons, Tab-wrap navigation in slash and agent dropdowns, /clear and /new chat commands, and async fs.promises migration for the CodebuffFileSystem interface across SDK run, initialSessionState, and CLI/npm-app/evals callers. eli5.text: When you run an agent that needs to read files from your project (like source code, documentation, or config files), it now uses the modern asynchronous file-reading system by default instead of the older synchronous one. This means background file discovery happens more smoothly with less chance of blocking or slowing things down, and you no longer need special casting code to make the file system work consistently across runs. Live today; nothing changes in how you call it.

ai.title: Structured error logging in CLI SDK client
ai.summary: New `cli/src/utils/error.ts` provides `ErrorOr<T>` result types and `getErrorObject` to normalize exceptions into serializable objects. `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` uses `getErrorObject` to pass structured error data to `logger.error` when `SDK client.run()` fails. Scope limited to CLI utilities and message hook. Non-Error throws fallback to stringified message with default 'Error' name.

eli5.text: When the chat tool runs into a problem talking to the AI assistant, it now logs the error details in a clear, organized way instead of dumping a messy technical error message. If you ever had to ask for help debugging a failed chat, you'll now get a cleaner report with the error type, message, and where it happened, rather than a jumble of system text. The change is live today and only affects what gets recorded behind the scenes when something goes wrong.

eli5.text: The Freebuff SDK has been updated to make file handling faster and to give you clearer, more understandable error messages when something goes wrong. Your projects will now load and scan their own files using a modern, built-in method behind the scenes, which makes discovering your project's structure and any saved knowledge files quicker and more reliable. When the assistant runs into a problem and can't finish a task, you'll now see a clean, readable summary of what failed instead of a confusing technical crash log. Upgrading means your coding sessions will start up more smoothly thanks to the improved file scanning, and if anything ever goes wrong, you can understand why at a glance. It's like tuning up your car's engine for a faster, smoother ride, plus adding a clearer dashboard when something needs your attention.

ai.title: CLI tools registry refactors message rendering
ai.summary: Tool rendering moves to `cli/src/components/tools/` with a central registry. `message-block.tsx` now calls `renderToolComponent` from `tools/registry` instead of `getToolRenderConfig` from deleted `tool-renderer.tsx`. Individual tool components like `code-search.tsx` and `list-directory.tsx` define rendering logic via `defineToolComponent`. Scope: CLI components only; no model or API changes.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a tool like searching your code, the CLI used to have one central place that decided how every tool's results were displayed, and each tool's display rules were mixed in with that place. The display logic for each tool has now been moved into its own separate folder so that each tool (like code search or listing directory contents) describes how it should look on its own, and the main message panel now simply asks a central list which tool should handle the display. A reader would notice nothing visually different today, but the system is now set up so plugins or extensions can register their own custom ways of showing tool results.
